root.label: Brookings assesses implementation lessons for place-based innovation awards

events.label: Brookings assesses implementation lessons for place-based innovation awards

slots.name: new coalitions
slots.sentence: Across the Engines and Tech Hubs programs, July’s announcements add 18 new coalitions to the broader map of place-based innovation investments, representing a diversity of emerging technologies.

slots.name: initial funding
slots.sentence: Each of the 12 new Engines will receive $15 million in federal funding over their first two years.

slots.name: Marshall Fire acreage
slots.sentence: Colorado and Wyoming’s ASCEND Engine, for example, recognized it had advanced research and innovation assets in sensing and prediction technologies that could mitigate environmental disasters such as the Marshall Fire, which devastated 6,000 acres in Colorado’s Front Range in 2021.

slots.name: seed subawards
slots.sentence: Through six “seed” and seven “scale” subawards , which were selected in a competitive request-for-proposals (RFP) process, FUEL tested programs with a wide range of recipients, including industry partners, nonprofit service providers, K-8 school districts, and community and technical colleges.

slots.name: portfolio regions
slots.sentence: Across these three programs, there are now over 50 U.S. regions responsible for delivering on the national place-based innovation experiment.

slots.name: CHIPS Act passage date
slots.sentence: Four years since the passage of the CHIPS and Science Act, the era of place-based federal investment that legislation established continues.

slots.name: innovation investment waves
slots.sentence: From federal programs to a national portfolio July’s new awards represent a third wave of ambitious place-based, tech-led economic development, following 2022’s Build Back Better Regional Challenge grants and the inaugural class of Engines and Tech Hubs in 2024.
